ko.executive_summary: AI data center demand is driving optical communications and silicon photonics adoption, with Tower Semiconductor and STMicroelectronics capitalizing on the buildout. Market participants including traditional suppliers like 3M are repositioning around photonic AI accelerators.
key_facts: Tower Semiconductor guides to $2 billion annual revenue
Tower Semiconductor's stock previously retreated 42% before recovery
Silicon photonics emerging as enabling technology for AI workloads
STMicroelectronics benefiting from AI and industrial demand surge
3M entering AI data center photonics sector
U.S. Photonic AI Accelerators market projected to 2035

implications.text: Silicon photonics integration for data centers is accelerating as AI infrastructure demands higher-bandwidth interconnects and lower latencies than traditional optics.
Specialized pure-play foundries (Tower) and broad-based suppliers (STMicroelectronics, 3M) are converging on photonics; market winners likely those with proven process capability at scale.
Chip market splitting into AI and non-AI segments; optical/photonic suppliers seeing disproportionate upside from hyperscaler capex concentration.

ko.counterpoint: Headlines lack specifics on CPO transceiver speeds, form factors, or customer wins; revenue guidance and stock movement are financial proxies rather than direct evidence of technology adoption or competitive positioning.
